question: Why might private clinics push for more injections in a fee-for-service system?

options.A: Government subsidies pay hospitals more for oral pills.
options.B: Insurance companies strictly forbid giving prescriptions for tablets.
options.C: Injections and related supplies allow them to charge higher fees.
options.D: Needles and syringes are completely free for medical facilities.

explanation: Financial gain drives unnecessary injections when clinics profit from charging extra for procedural administration and supplies. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary action a nurse should perform before preparing any medication?

options.A: Check the patient's room temperature
options.B: Ask the family member what drugs the patient takes
options.C: Verify the order against the medication administration record
options.D: Wash the medication trolley with bleach

explanation: Comparing the medication order against the official administration record prevents medication errors and ensures patient safety. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is a functional referral system necessary for family planning clients?

options.A: It ensures safe, continuous care when a client needs specialized services
options.B: It allows primary health centers to perform major surgical sterilizations
options.C: It guarantees that clients never have to pay for their contraceptive drugs
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses to provide health education at primary clinics

explanation: Referrals link primary care clinics to advanced facilities, ensuring clients get appropriate treatment without dropping out of care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h1)

question: What is the emergency procedure where a tiny cut is made in the neck membrane to open a blocked airway?

options.A: Removing a tracheostomy tube
options.B: Bronchoscopy
options.C: Cricothyroidotomy
options.D: Thoracentesis

explanation: A cricothyroidotomy is an emergency lifesaving move. When nothing else works and the upper airway is fully shut, healthcare providers cut through the cricothyroid membrane to create a direct path for air.

question: What is the main goal of turning cystine into cysteine-drug complexes?

options.A: The drug permanently neutralizes all urinary calcium
options.B: The complexes completely stop the kidneys from producing urine
options.C: The body can reabsorb the new complexes safely in the loop of Henle
options.D: The new complexes dissolve much more easily in urine

explanation: By changing the chemical structure, the drug makes cystine soluble so it can comfortably wash out in the urine instead of forming painful stones.

question: Why are people with long-term HIV at a higher risk for heart disease?

options.A: Patients universally develop severe iron-deficiency anemia
options.B: Low red blood cell counts force the heart to beat faster
options.C: Persistent systemic inflammation damages blood vessels
options.D: The virus directly destroys heart muscle tissue daily

explanation: Ongoing immune activation keeps the body in a state of low-level inflammation, which over time can damage blood vessels and raise heart disease risk.

question: A patient starts tensing their muscles and pulls away when you try to examine their shoulder. What is the best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Administer a strong painkiller immediately without a doctor's order
options.B: Document that the patient is uncooperative and end the shift assessment
options.C: Stop, explain what you are doing, and encourage relaxation to reduce guarding
options.D: Hold the arm down firmly and finish the examination quickly

explanation: Tension and protective muscle guarding block accurate assessment of joint movement and strength, so reassuring the patient is vital. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h2)

question: A patient with large fibroids complains of constant pelvic pressure and constipation. Why is she likely constipated?

options.A: Side effects from high estrogen levels
options.B: A complete blockage of the small intestine
options.C: Pressure from the fibroids on the rectum
options.D: Severe inflammation of the uterine lining

explanation: An enlarged uterus and bulky fibroids can press backward against the rectum, making bowel movements difficult. Simple anatomy in action!

question: A scared patient asks if the metal pins will hurt going into their head. What should you say?

options.A: You will feel a sharp pain, but it will go away as soon as the weights are hung.
options.B: Do not worry, the pins are very small and just rest on top of your hair.
options.C: Most patients are asleep during the whole process so they never feel anything.
options.D: The doctor will numb your scalp with medicine first so you won't feel sharp pain.

explanation: Always be honest and comforting! Letting them know the doctor will numb the area first builds great trust and calms their nerves.

question: At what angle do you typically insert a subcutaneous needle when using a 5/8-inch needle on an average patient?

options.A: 120 degrees
options.B: 15 degrees
options.C: 45 or 90 degrees
options.D: 180 degrees

explanation: Spot on! Depending on the needle size and how much skin fold you have, 45 or 90 degrees are your two go-to angles.

question: A patient is admitted with suspected celiac disease. Which specific blood test does the nurse expect the healthcare provider to order first?

options.A: Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA)
options.B: Serum amylase and lipase levels
options.C: Anti-tissue transglutaminase (tTG) antibodies
options.D: Blood urea nitrogen and creatinine

explanation: Serologic antibody testing for anti-tTG is the standard primary screening tool used to detect celiac disease in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is the main cause of an ischemic stroke?

options.A: Sudden systemic drop in normal body temperature
options.B: Uncontrolled electrical discharge across the motor cortex
options.C: Rupture of a weakened blood vessel inside the brain tissue
options.D: Occlusion of a cerebral artery by a thrombus or embolus

explanation: An ischemic stroke happens when a blood clot blocks a brain vessel, cutting off the oxygen and nutrients that part of the brain needs.

question: What is the main job of a healthy fallopian tube?

options.A: To filter waste products from the pelvic cavity
options.B: To provide a pathway for the egg and the site for fertilization
options.C: To produce female hormones like estrogen and progesterone
options.D: To nourish the developing embryo throughout the entire pregnancy

explanation: Think of the fallopian tube as the highway where the egg travels and meets sperm for fertilization. Simple and straightforward!

question: Which of these side-to-side measurements is the wider one across a baby's skull?

options.A: The biparietal diameter
options.B: The bitemporal diameter
options.C: Neither is used in obstetrics
options.D: Both measure exactly the same

explanation: The biparietal diameter stretches across the widest part of the parietal bones, making it broader than the bitemporal measurement across the temples.

question: What complication can develop in a patient who suffers from severe, unmanaged fear throughout a long hospital stay?

options.A: Complete immunity to all future bacterial infections
options.B: Post-traumatic stress symptoms related to the medical experience
options.C: Instant recovery from chronic respiratory illnesses
options.D: Permanent loss of the sense of taste and smell

explanation: Well done! Extreme, unmanaged distress during medical care can unfortunately leave long-lasting psychological scars.

question: What is the main goal of vestibular rehabilitation therapy?

options.A: To permanently eliminate all physical movement of the head
options.B: To train the central nervous system to compensate for inner ear deficits
options.C: To surgically replace the delicate structures of the inner ear
options.D: To increase blood pressure and prevent fainting episodes

explanation: Spot on! Vestibular therapy uses smart exercises to help the brain learn how to handle balance signals better, even if the inner ear isn't working at 100%.

question: Why is tracking data over time with a wearable better than a single blood pressure check at the clinic?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to manually record any vital signs
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will take all prescribed medications
options.D: It captures daily trends and avoids single-visit anxiety spikes

explanation: Ever get nervous seeing a doctor in a white coat? Wearables show real everyday trends without hospital stress getting in the way.

question: Why is folic acid given to women before and during early pregnancy?

options.A: To stop excessive bleeding during the third trimester
options.B: To speed up the onset of active labor pains
options.C: To cure maternal high blood pressure permanently
options.D: To prevent neural tube defects in the developing baby

explanation: Correct! Folic acid is a little vitamin with a big job—it protects the baby's brain and spinal cord development in the early weeks.

question: When changing sheets for a bedridden patient who cannot get up, how should you handle the top covers?

options.A: Place the clean top sheet over the old one, then pull the old sheet out from underneath
options.B: Ask the patient to hold the dirty blanket up with both hands
options.C: Remove all covers completely, leaving the patient uncovered until the end
options.D: Strip the top of the bed first and replace sheets while the patient sits up

explanation: Spot on! Layering the clean cover over the old one before sliding the old one out keeps your patient warm and protects their privacy the whole time.

question: Which physical sign strongly indicates that a patient is developing phlebitis at their IV site?

options.A: Clear fluid leaks out from beneath the transparent dressing
options.B: The surrounding skin feels very cold and appears swollen
options.C: A red, warm, tender streak following the path of the vein
options.D: The infusion pump stops working and sounds an occlusion alarm

explanation: Phlebitis is vein inflammation, showing up as redness, warmth, and pain along the vessel path. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h8)

question: A new mother who just had a tear repaired with stitches (episiotomy) says she is soaking her private area in very hot water daily for pain. What is the major risk here?

options.A: Instantaneous regeneration of damaged muscle fibers
options.B: Complete prevention of postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Immediate closure of the surgical wound within minutes
options.D: Tissue maceration and delayed wound healing leading to infection

explanation: Fresh stitches need time to stay clean and dry. Soaking them in hot water makes the skin soggy (macerated), which slows down healing and lets germs in.

question: Why must the dropper be aimed away from the center nasal septum during instillation?

options.A: To block the airflow in both nostrils equally
options.B: To avoid injuring the delicate tissues and causing bleeding
options.C: To make sure the liquid enters the mouth directly
options.D: To prevent the dropper tip from bending

explanation: The nasal septum has a fragile blood supply that can easily bleed if scraped by a dropper tip. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h7)

question: What are the three main types of germs that cause sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Fungal, protozoal, and cellular toxins
options.B: Nutritional, bacterial, and hormonal elements
options.C: Genetic, environmental, and viral factors
options.D: Bacterial, viral, and parasitic agents

explanation: You'll often see these three! STIs are primarily caused by bacteria, viruses, and parasites. Knowing your enemy helps you educate your patients better.

question: Why is exogenous insulin therapy required for clients diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Their kidneys rapidly destroy all oral medications before they reach cells
options.B: Their stomach acid inactivates any dietary carbohydrates they consume
options.C: Their liver stores too much glycogen that oral pills cannot break down
options.D: Their pancreas has undergone autoimmune destruction and produces no insulin

explanation: Because Type 1 diabetes involves a total lack of internal insulin production, patients must receive insulin from an outside source to survive. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h6)

question: A patient is deeply sad over losing a pet, but friends tell them to just get another one. What kind of grief is this?

options.A: Anticipatory grief
options.B: Disenfranchised grief
options.C: Uncomplicated grief
options.D: Collective grief

explanation: Exactly! When people brush off a loss because they don't understand its value—like a pet—the person experiences disenfranchised grief because others don't validate their pain.

question: What is the main way frontline nurses and midwives help with tracking maternal mortality?

options.A: Publishing international epidemiological textbooks for medical schools
options.B: Conducting national population censuses every ten years
options.C: Designing mathematical algorithms for computer software models
options.D: Accurate and complete documentation in institutional delivery and admission registers

explanation: As a nurse or midwife, your daily job of properly writing down births, complications, and outcomes in hospital registers builds the foundation for all national data!

question: Which sign requires your immediate, urgent attention after a patient receives an intrapleural medication?

options.A: Mild local soreness around the chest tube insertion site
options.B: Anxiety about the upcoming hospital discharge date
options.C: Sudden respiratory distress and falling oxygen saturation
options.D: Low-grade fever developing twenty-four hours later

explanation: Safety first! Trouble breathing or dropping oxygen levels can mean a serious complication like a collapsed lung or severe spasm, so you must act fast.

question: What usually causes a Bartholin duct cyst to form?

options.A: Hormonal overproduction by the adrenal cortex
options.B: Blockage of the gland duct causing fluid to back up
options.C: Direct bacterial invasion from the urinary bladder
options.D: A genetic absence of the external genitalia glands

explanation: When the tiny tube (duct) leading from the Bartholin gland gets blocked, the fluid has nowhere to go and builds up into a cyst.

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of simple pregnancy heartburn?

options.A: Worsening discomfort after eating a large meal
options.B: A sour taste at the back of the throat
options.C: A burning feeling behind the breastbone
options.D: Crushing chest pain radiating to the jaw

explanation: Crushing jaw pain points toward heart trouble, not regular acid reflux. Good clinical spotting!

question: What specific details should a nurse include when charting newborn skull moulding?

options.A: The mother's exact pelvis shape and measurements
options.B: The degree of bone overlapping and presence of scalp lesions
options.C: The exact volume of blood lost by the mother
options.D: The specific brand of instruments used during delivery

explanation: You've got this! Good nursing notes focus on the baby's actual condition—how the bones are aligned and if there is any swelling or scratches on the scalp.

question: Which of these is a main reason a doctor would order a barium enema?

options.A: Elevated liver enzymes and yellow skin jaundice
options.B: Unexplained chronic diarrhea and rectal bleeding
options.C: Severe dehydration from upper GI bleeding
options.D: Sharp lower right belly pain caused by appendicitis

explanation: Doctors use barium enemas to investigate ongoing lower bowel problems like bleeding or long-term changes in stool patterns.

question: A patient is pacing the ward rapidly, breathing fast, and speaking in a frantic rush. What should you do first?

options.A: Administer a strong oral stimulant to boost their energy.
options.B: Move the patient to a quiet area and speak in a calm, reassuring tone.
options.C: Leave the patient alone until they calm down on their own.
options.D: Ask the patient to sit down and fill out a detailed anxiety questionnaire.

explanation: Lowering the noise and distractions around the patient—paired with your own calm presence—does wonders to bring their anxiety down.

question: An IV bag of 1,000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a pump. What is the hourly rate?

options.A: 150 mL/hr
options.B: 80 mL/hr
options.C: 125 mL/hr
options.D: 100 mL/hr

explanation: Divide total volume by total hours: 1,000 mL ÷ 8 hours = 125 mL/hr.

question: Why are transdermal patches unique compared to standard topical creams?

options.A: They deliver a controlled, continuous systemic dose of medication over a long period
options.B: They only work if rubbed vigorously into the dermal layer of the skin
options.C: They are completely water-soluble and wash off easily with light sweat
options.D: They are applied exclusively to open wounds to speed up local cellular healing

explanation: Transdermal patches utilize a special rate-limiting membrane to slowly release medication into the bloodstream over several hours or days. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h3)

question: How does a Root Cause Analysis differ from simply blaming an individual worker?

options.A: It focuses exclusively on financial losses rather than clinical outcomes
options.B: It investigates underlying systemic flaws rather than stopping at personal fault
options.C: It ensures that the guilty employee is fired immediately without appeal
options.D: It hides safety mistakes from hospital management and regulatory bodies

explanation: Root Cause Analysis asks 'Why did this happen?' instead of 'Who did this?'. It digs deep into workflow, equipment, and communication to fix the real problem.

question: How many major components typically make up a comprehensive neurological assessment?

options.A: Eight
options.B: Twelve
options.C: Two
options.D: Five

explanation: The standard exam covers mental status, cranial nerves, motor system, sensory system, and reflexes. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is a common social penalty for a family that refuses FGM in a pro-FGM community?

options.A: Severe ostracism and social isolation
options.B: Mandatory community service penalties
options.C: Permanent banishment from public schooling
options.D: Immediate imprisonment by local chiefs

explanation: That's right. Families who break this tradition often face intense rejection and loneliness from people around them.

question: Why are elderly patients much more prone to skin tears?

options.A: Their skin cells regenerate at an unusually rapid pace
options.B: Their blood circulation is much faster than in younger adults
options.C: Their epidermis thins and subcutaneous fat decreases
options.D: Their sweat glands produce excessive amounts of natural oils

explanation: Well done! As people age, their skin naturally thins out and loses its soft padding, making it much more delicate.

question: What is the primary purpose of secondary neurological prevention?

options.A: Catching disease early and halting its progress
options.B: Performing major neurosurgery in emergency rooms
options.C: Preventing people from ever starting to smoke
options.D: Teaching chronic patients how to use a wheelchair

explanation: Secondary prevention is all about early catch-up. Through quick screenings and fast intervention, we catch health issues early to limit lasting damage.

question: Which care delivery system assigns specific tasks, like giving out meds or doing wound dressings, to different nurses?

options.A: Functional nursing
options.B: Total patient care
options.C: Case management
options.D: Primary nursing

explanation: Spot on! Functional nursing divides the workload by specific tasks across the whole ward, like a factory assembly line for care.

question: Which protozoal infection is mainly spread through contaminated food and water, often causing dysentery?

options.A: Entamoeba histolytica
options.B: Trypanosoma brucei
options.C: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.D: Plasmodium falciparum

explanation: Great job! Ingesting Entamoeba histolytica cysts through dirty water or food can lead to painful amebic dysentery.

question: What is the main goal of food and nutrition when caring for a patient receiving palliative care?

options.A: Reversing the underlying terminal disease
options.B: Building muscle mass and healing wounds
options.C: Extending life by forcing high calorie intake
options.D: Promoting comfort and quality of life

explanation: Great job thinking about holistic care! In palliative care, we focus on what brings the patient peace and enjoyment rather than trying to reverse the disease or force weight gain.

question: Why is a complete blood count (CBC) useful when checking a patient with an unknown fever?

options.A: It measures exact prostaglandin levels in the blood
options.B: It shows the exact brain set point
options.C: It helps tell bacterial and viral infections apart using white blood cells
options.D: It tells you which mosquito species bit the patient

explanation: You're doing great! High white blood cells usually point to bacteria, helping us choose the right care.

question: What do we call the joint right at the front where the pubic bones meet?

options.A: Pubic symphysis
options.B: Acetabulum
options.C: Lumbosacral joint
options.D: Sacroiliac joint

explanation: Great job! The pubic symphysis is simply the cartilaginous joint joining the right and left pubic bones right at the front midline.

question: Why must you let the skin antiseptic dry completely before starting an IV stick?

options.A: To allow the chemical to fully destroy microorganisms on the skin
options.B: To ensure the vein stays plump and easy to palpate
options.C: To prevent the sticky dressing from sliding off wet skin
options.D: To stop the client from feeling a sharp burning sensation

explanation: Patience pays off! Antiseptics like chlorhexidine need a little contact and drying time to actually kill the germs on the skin before you puncture it.

question: What causes the intense, driving itch of a scabies mite infestation?

options.A: The mites block blood flow and cause minor tissue death
options.B: An allergic reaction to the mites' waste and proteins in the skin
options.C: The mites chew directly through deep nerve endings
options.D: The mites secrete histamine directly from their mouths

explanation: That severe scabies itch isn't just from crawling—it's your immune system throwing an allergic reaction to the proteins and feces the mites leave behind in their tunnels.

question: Why do we tell patients to elevate a sprained ankle above the level of the heart?

options.A: It increases arterial blood flow to speed up ligament fiber regeneration
options.B: Elevation prevents the development of systemic blood clots in the leg
options.C: Gravity helps drain excess fluid and reduce swelling at the injury site
options.D: It relaxes the calf muscles so the bone fracture can heal properly

explanation: Elevation uses gravity to pull extra fluid away from the injured area, helping to bring down that painful swelling.

question: What is the main job of the sticky electrode pads on an AED?

options.A: To monitor the patient's blood pressure and oxygen levels
options.B: To warm up the patient's skin before the shock is given
options.C: To sense the heart rhythm and deliver the electrical shock
options.D: To manually pump blood through the chest cavity

explanation: Think of the pads as the bridge between the patient and the machine: they read what the heart is doing and carry the shock safely into the body.

question: Why must a chest drainage system always stay lower than the patient's chest level?

options.A: To ensure the suction motor runs quietly without disturbing the patient
options.B: To use gravity effectively and prevent fluid from flowing backward into the pleural space
options.C: To make it easier for the patient to ambulate around the room
options.D: To prevent the water-seal chamber from evaporating too quickly

explanation: Gravity is our best friend here; keeping the collection box down ensures fluid drains away from the patient, not back into them. You've got a bright future in ward nursing!

question: Why is asphyxia treated as a sudden medical emergency rather than a chronic disease?

options.A: It can only be treated with long-term oral medications
options.B: It only happens inside hospital operating rooms
options.C: It happens because something abruptly stops breathing, needing instant help
options.D: It develops slowly over several months without symptoms

explanation: Asphyxia isn't a long-term illness; it's an urgent crisis where something blocks breathing right now, so every second counts for rescue!

question: What special tools do cancer cells use to break through surrounding tissue barriers?

options.A: Matrix metalloproteinases
options.B: Gastric digestive pepsins
options.C: Liver clotting factors
options.D: Insulin receptor enzymes

explanation: MMPs act like little scissors or chemical drills, helping cancer cells chew through the matrix and invade surrounding tissue.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard emergency maneuver used during shoulder dystocia?

options.A: applying downward pressure above the maternal pubic bone
options.B: flexing the maternal legs sharply up toward her abdomen
options.C: administering strong uterine relaxants intravenously
options.D: summoning immediate pediatric and obstetric assistance

explanation: Spot on! For shoulder dystocia, we use physical repositioning (like the McRoberts maneuver) and suprapubic pressure rather than IV uterine relaxants.

question: What is the main feature of self-directed violence?

options.A: It involves organized groups fighting for political power
options.B: The victim and the perpetrator are the same person
options.C: It is always done by close family members
options.D: It happens only in crowded city areas

explanation: Exactly! Self-directed violence means actions someone inflicts on themselves, such as self-harm or suicide attempts.

question: What is the main job of resuscitative equipment in the ward?

options.A: To provide routine daily patient hygiene care
options.B: To monitor long-term chronic wound healing
options.C: To manage sudden cardiac or respiratory arrest
options.D: To deliver oral medications during meals

explanation: You've got this! Resuscitative tools are kept ready specifically for emergencies when a patient stops breathing or their heart stops. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h1)

question: What big challenge do family members often face when they care round-the-clock for a relative with a severe physical disability?

options.A: Permanent immunity from chronic lifestyle diseases
options.B: Caregiver burnout and emotional exhaustion
options.C: Sudden loss of personal interest in healthcare
options.D: Automatic financial compensation from the state

explanation: Well done! Looking after someone 24/7 takes a heavy toll. Caregivers need care and support too so they don't burn out.

question: What is the best dietary advice for a mother who is exclusively breastfeeding?

options.A: Strictly avoid all dairy products
options.B: Increase daily food and water intake
options.C: Avoid eating green leafy vegetables
options.D: Reduce water intake so milk isn't watery

explanation: Making breast milk takes a lot of energy and water! Mums need good nutritious meals and plenty of clean water to stay strong.

question: What is the most common spark that sets off a sudden metabolic or endocrine emergency?

options.A: A sudden physical stressor or infection
options.B: A sudden drop in room temperature
options.C: Drinking too much water too fast
options.D: Eating too much high-fat food

explanation: You've got this! When infections or physical stress hit the body, they demand extra energy, easily pushing a delicate hormone balance right over the edge into an emergency.

question: What is the main reason doctors order a daily 'sedation vacation' for a ventilated patient?

options.A: To let the ventilator machine calibrate its internal sensors
options.B: To allow the nursing staff to take a scheduled meal break
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of medications in the unit
options.D: To evaluate the patient's neurological status and readiness for weaning

explanation: Pausing sedation for a short while lets us check how the patient's brain is doing and see if they are strong enough to start breathing on their own. Brilliant teamwork!

question: In most parts of Nigeria, under what single major condition is an abortion legally permitted?

options.A: When both parents agree in writing before the first trimester
options.B: When the woman is below the age of consent
options.C: When the pregnancy results from an act of sexual assault
options.D: When the procedure is strictly necessary to save the woman's life

explanation: Nigerian law is quite strict, usually only allowing an abortion if the continuation of the pregnancy directly threatens the mother's life. It's an important legal boundary every nurse practicing here should know.

question: Which quick bedside test checks for low calcium by tapping gently on the facial nerve?

options.A: Chvostek's sign
options.B: Brudzinski's sign
options.C: Homan's sign
options.D: Trousseau's sign

explanation: That's Chvostek's sign! Tap right on the cheek/facial nerve; if calcium is too low, the facial muscles will twitch uncontrollably. A classic physical assessment trick!

question: Where is the safest place to give a vitamin K injection to a full-term newborn?

options.A: Ventral gluteal muscle
options.B: Vastus lateralis muscle
options.C: Deltoid muscle of the arm
options.D: Dorsogluteal muscle

explanation: The vastus lateralis in the outer thigh is the go-to spot! It's well-developed in newborns and keeps them safe from major nerves and blood vessels.

question: Which sign might tell you a patient has developed a collapsed lung (pneumothorax) after a liver biopsy?

options.A: Inability to control their bladder
options.B: Sudden trouble breathing and reduced breath sounds on the right side
options.C: Yellow skin and eyes appearing within an hour
options.D: Painful bruising right on the skin puncture site

explanation: You nailed it! Since the liver sits right under the lung, a misplaced needle can let air into the chest cavity, leading to breathing trouble on that side.

question: What is a very common emotional challenge faced by people who survive severe road crashes?

options.A: Complete emotional numbness to joy
options.B: Increased physical stamina
options.C: Post-traumatic stress disorder
options.D: Enhanced memory retention

explanation: Survivors of violent crashes often deal with lingering emotional trauma, anxiety, and flashbacks, known as PTSD.

question: What is the primary goal of using strict aseptic technique during invasive procedures?

options.A: To neutralize chemical toxins released by resident skin flora
options.B: To eliminate all pathogenic microorganisms from the sterile field
options.C: To reduce the total number of bacteria on non-porous furniture
options.D: To remove visible dirt and oil from the patient's outer skin

explanation: Aseptic technique aims to protect susceptible body sites by ensuring zero pathogens are introduced during invasive tasks. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which sociological theory suggests that older adults remain happier and healthier when they stay busy and socially involved?

options.A: Free radical theory
options.B: Activity theory
options.C: Disengagement theory
options.D: Wear-and-tear theory

explanation: Activity theory proposes that staying socially active and maintaining roles promotes well-being in older age. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h3)

question: A mother brings her 3-day-old baby to the clinic with severe jaundice and mentions storing baby clothes with traditional camphor. What likely caused this?

options.A: An allergic reaction to the scent of the fabric softener used
options.B: Blockage of the newborn bile ducts caused by dust inhalation
options.C: Direct contamination of the skin by toxic chemicals in the air
options.D: Oxidative destruction of red blood cells in a baby with an enzyme defect

explanation: Camphor fumes from stored clothes can trigger rapid breakdown of red blood cells (hemolysis) in babies with G6PD deficiency. This is a very important health education point for mothers in Nigeria!

question: What is the main goal of the DASH diet for someone with high blood pressure?

options.A: To increase potassium, calcium, and fiber while reducing sodium
options.B: To replace all fluid intake with specialized herbal teas
options.C: To encourage rapid weight loss through strict calorie counting
options.D: To eliminate all carbohydrates from the daily meal plan

explanation: DASH focuses on whole foods packed with good minerals like potassium and calcium while cutting back on salt to protect the heart.

question: How can severe kidney problems in an expectant mother directly hurt her baby?

options.A: By passing high levels of urea directly into the fetal stomach
options.B: By reducing blood supply and nutrient delivery across the placenta
options.C: By triggering early closure of the fetal cardiac chambers
options.D: By increasing the amount of amniotic fluid to dangerous levels

explanation: When the mother's kidneys and blood pressure struggle, the placenta doesn't get enough blood flow, which means the baby gets less of what it needs to grow strong.

question: Why does the examiner systematically trace the retinal blood vessel branches during the assessment?

options.A: To push any trapped fluid away from the delicate optic nerve head
options.B: To measure the exact pulse rate of blood flowing through the brain
options.C: To check for normal branching patterns, caliber changes, and color
options.D: To stimulate the retina into producing more natural lubricating tears

options.C: It delivers a precise and controlled concentration of oxygen.
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any humidification.

explanation: Venturi masks use clever color-coded adapters to give an exact percentage of oxygen, keeping vulnerable COPD patients safe.

question: Why must wrapped instrument trays be loaded loosely inside a steam sterilizer?

options.A: To allow steam to circulate freely around every package
options.B: To stop the external indicator tape from melting off
options.C: To prevent the heavy metal trays from breaking the door
options.D: To make unloading faster for the nursing assistant

explanation: If the packs are crammed too tightly together, the steam can't reach every surface, leaving pockets where germs can survive.

question: Why are ACE inhibitor medications often given to kidney disease patients even if their blood pressure is completely normal?

options.A: They stimulate the bone marrow to produce extra white blood cells.
options.B: They absorb extra phosphorus directly from the gastrointestinal tract.
options.C: They reduce pressure inside the glomeruli and decrease protein leakage.
options.D: They dissolve calcium deposits that form inside the renal tubules.

explanation: Think of ACE inhibitors as pressure-relieving valves for the nephrons. By easing the internal filtering pressure, they protect the kidneys from wearing out faster.

question: Why should nurses avoid vague phrases like 'skin looks infected' in professional charting?

options.A: It slows down the discharge planning process for the medical team
options.B: It prevents the patient from reading their own medical chart history
options.C: It automatically violates hospital legal policies regarding privacy protection
options.D: It lacks the specific, objective details required to evaluate treatment efficacy

explanation: Vague words don't give enough detail. Saying '1cm red area with pus' tells the whole team much more than just 'infected'.

question: A patient with a new leg cast complains of severe, burning pain that does not respond to prescribed pain medication and has pale toes. What is the nurse's priority action?

options.A: Instruct the patient to exercise their toes more vigorously
options.B: Apply a heating pad directly over the tight plaster cast
options.C: Notify the doctor immediately for signs of compartment syndrome
options.D: Wait patiently until the next scheduled pain medication time

explanation: Unrelenting pain and poor circulation under a cast can signal dangerous pressure build-up, requiring urgent medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h8)

question: What percentage of tiny particles must an N95 respirator filter out?

options.A: Exactly 50 percent
options.B: At least 95 percent
options.C: 100 percent without exception
options.D: Up to 80 percent maximum

explanation: The '95' in N95 simply means it catches a minimum of 95 percent of test particles. Simple and reliable!

question: Which type of medication is usually prescribed to help strengthen bones in patients with osteoporosis?

options.A: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Bisphosphonates
options.C: Inhaled bronchodilators
options.D: Sedative hypnotics

explanation: Bisphosphonates act like a brake on bone breakdown, helping the body hold onto its bone density.

question: What is the name of the thick, yellowish milk produced in the first few days after birth?

options.A: Foremilk
options.B: Colostrum
options.C: Hindmilk
options.D: Transition milk

explanation: Colostrum is the first milk produced after birth, packed with high concentrations of protective antibodies for the newborn. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h3)

question: A patient in a rural community stops coming for clinic refills because transport fare is more expensive than the drugs. What barrier is this?

options.A: Excessive complexity of the drug regimen
options.B: Patient denial of the disease diagnosis
options.C: Acute adverse drug reactions
options.D: Geographical and financial barriers

explanation: Distance and travel costs create heavy hurdles that block patients from getting their regular medication supplies.

question: A patient with new hearing aids complains that everyday sounds are way too loud and annoying. What should you tell them?

options.A: Advise the patient to stop wearing the hearing aids permanently
options.B: Explain that the brain needs time to adjust to amplified environmental sounds
options.C: Tell the patient to turn the volume control up even higher for clarity
options.D: Acknowledge that the device is broken and needs immediate replacement

explanation: It's totally normal! When someone hasn't heard everyday sounds clearly in a while, their brain gets overwhelmed at first. Give it time and patience.

question: What is an important nursing task for the AED right after a emergency code is over?

options.A: Store the used electrode pads in the patient's bedside cabinet.
options.B: Clean the unit, restock supplies, and return it to its storage station.
options.C: Take the AED apart to clean the internal computer processor.
options.D: Send the AED back to the manufacturer for factory resetting.

explanation: Once the excitement settles, make sure the AED is wiped down, restocked with fresh pads, and put right back in its place so it's ready for the next shift.

question: Why do patients with newly discovered vulval cysts often feel very anxious?

options.A: Doctors usually misdiagnose it as a severe systemic infection
options.B: It automatically causes total infertility in young women
options.C: They frequently mistake the lump for a cancerous growth
options.D: The condition always requires immediate emergency surgery

explanation: Finding any unexplained lump can be scary! Patients often worry about cancer right away until a nurse or doctor calmly explains that it is benign.

question: Which of the following is checked during a social and practical support assessment?

options.A: Safety of the home environment and availability of caregivers
options.B: The exact microscopic cell count found in blood lab results
options.C: The specific brand of pain medication prescribed by the doctor
options.D: The patient's personal religious beliefs and church history

explanation: We check living conditions and who is around to help out, making sure the patient will be safe and supported at home.

question: Which biopsy tool uses a tiny round, cookie-cutter blade to take a full-depth core of skin?

options.A: Punch biopsy
options.B: Excisional biopsy
options.C: Incisional biopsy
options.D: Shave biopsy

explanation: Think of a punch biopsy like a tiny apple corer! It uses a small, hollow circular blade to get a clean sample going through all the skin layers.

question: What makes an expected outcome (goal) well-written?

options.A: It must be measurable and time-bound
options.B: It should describe what the nurse will do
options.C: It should be as broad as possible
options.D: It must focus on hospital routines

explanation: Goals need clear targets and deadlines (like 'patient will walk to the door by tomorrow') so you can easily tell if they were actually reached.

question: Which body area absorbs topical medications the fastest, often requiring a lower concentration?

options.A: The face and skin folds
options.B: The soles of the feet
options.C: The palms of the hands
options.D: The thick skin of the back

explanation: Thin skin areas absorb medications much quicker, increasing the risk of irritation if the drug is too strong. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h2)

question: As the baby's head extends to be born, which bone acts as the pivot point?

options.A: The pubic symphysis
options.B: The coccyx bone
options.C: The ischial spine
options.D: The maternal sacrum

explanation: Correct! The baby's head pivots right under the mother's pubic bone, allowing it to lift upward and out into the world.

question: How do bureaucratic silos hurt community health networks?

options.A: They eliminate all communication costs between health facilities
options.B: They prevent organizations from sharing data and coordinating their community interventions effectively
options.C: They automatically increase the number of trained midwives in rural areas
options.D: They force government ministries to merge with private pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Spot on! When agencies work in separate bubbles, resources get wasted and important gaps pop up in patient care.

question: What common foot problem does a footboard primarily prevent in patients who are on bed rest?

options.A: Deep vein thrombosis
options.B: Pressure ulcers on the heels
options.C: Hypostatic pneumonia
options.D: Foot drop

explanation: Brilliant! A footboard holds the feet in a natural upright position, stopping the Achilles tendon from tightening up and causing permanent foot drop.

question: A patient finishes metronidazole for amebic dysentery but skips the luminal agent. What is the biggest risk?

options.A: Immediate development of permanent kidney failure
options.B: Severe permanent discoloration of the skin
options.C: Total immunity to all future bacterial infections
options.D: Relapse of the infection from surviving cysts in the gut

explanation: Exactly! Leftover cysts in the gut can hatch later and bring the infection right back, even if the patient felt better temporarily.

question: An enlarged prostate gland that blocks urine flow from the bladder falls under which category of acute renal failure?

options.A: Prerenal
options.B: Postrenal
options.C: Systemic
options.D: Intrarenal

explanation: Postrenal causes involve any blockage that prevents urine from leaving the body after it is formed by the kidneys. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h2)

question: A patient who had a barium enema yesterday hasn't passed any stool yet and now has worsening belly pain. What should you do?

options.A: Tell them to wait another three days before worrying
options.B: Notify the doctor right away, because trapped barium can cause a serious blockage
options.C: Reassure them that white stools take a whole week to clear
options.D: Advise them to eat a heavy meal to push the stool down

explanation: If barium gets stuck and the patient has belly pain, it can lead to a bowel impaction or blockage. Quick reporting keeps the patient safe!

question: What is the primary goal of routine HIV testing during antenatal care (PMTCT programs)?

options.A: To prevent transmission of the virus from mother to child
options.B: To replace standard antenatal blood pressure checks
options.C: To determine eligibility for paid maternity leave benefits
options.D: To enforce mandatory quarantine for pregnant women

explanation: You nailed it! Testing mums early lets them start treatment so they can drastically lower the chance of passing the virus to their baby.

question: You notice some insulin vials have been sitting on a warm desk for hours. What should you do?

options.A: Dilute the warm insulin with sterile water to restore its cold temperature
options.B: Consult the pharmacy or discard the compromised vials according to policy
options.C: Return them immediately to the patient refrigerator without checking
options.D: Administer them quickly before the expiration date arrives next month

explanation: You nailed it. Insulin is sensitive to heat and loses its potency when left out. Always check with pharmacy or follow safety rules rather than risking a patient's dose.

question: What is a vital nursing duty right after giving an antidote to a poisoned patient?

options.A: Stopping all cardiac monitoring to let the patient rest
options.B: Discharging the patient immediately if they feel better
options.C: Restricting all oral fluids for the next 48 hours
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and watching for secondary complications

explanation: You're doing great! Antidotes can sometimes wear off before the poison is completely gone from the body, so close monitoring of vital signs is a must to keep the patient safe.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse must do if a patient reacts badly to an IV medication?

options.A: Give an oral allergy tablet
options.B: Write down the exact time in the chart
options.C: Leave the room to find the doctor
options.D: Stop the medication infusion right away

explanation: Safety first! Stopping the drug immediately keeps any more of the bad stuff from entering the patient's body.

question: What is the main reason for frequently cleaning high-touch surfaces in an isolation room?

options.A: To prevent germs from surviving on objects and spreading
options.B: To prevent medical equipment from rusting
options.C: To make the floor shiny and slip-resistant
options.D: To keep the room smelling fresh for visitors

explanation: Pathogens can live on dry surfaces for hours or days, making regular disinfection vital to stopping indirect spread. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h6)

question: Why do nurses write and share research reports?

options.A: To criticize current hospital management policies
options.B: To fulfill a graduation requirement without clinical use
options.C: To promote personal medical opinions to the public
options.D: To communicate new knowledge for evidence-based practice

explanation: You got this! Research turns everyday clinical questions into clear evidence we can use to give our patients the best care possible.

question: Who typically leads a peer-led HIV support group?

options.A: A licensed medical doctor or surgeon
options.B: A hospital laboratory technician
options.C: A veteran community member living with HIV
options.D: A government health policy maker

explanation: Peer-led groups are guided by individuals who share the lived experience of managing the condition successfully. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h2)

question: A community health nurse wants to reduce head injuries among local commercial motorcycle riders. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Fines for patients who report to the hospital injured
options.B: Closing down all commercial transport businesses
options.C: Conducting safety campaigns on proper helmet use with riders
options.D: Waiting in the clinic to treat victims as they arrive

explanation: Working directly with transport riders to promote safety education and helmet use is a proven way to prevent severe head trauma.

question: Why is mixed feeding (breast milk plus other foods or water) discouraged for infants exposed to HIV?

options.A: It damages the infant's immature gut lining and increases transmission risk.
options.B: It is too expensive for families living in rural communities.
options.C: It prevents the baby from ever developing taste preferences.
options.D: It causes immediate allergic reactions in all newborn infants.

explanation: Introducing other liquids or foods irritates the baby's gut wall, making it much easier for the HIV virus in breast milk to enter the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h7)

question: What is a defining characteristic of a modern intensive care unit?

options.A: Low staffing levels because patients are mostly stable
options.B: High nurse-to-patient ratios and specialized life support equipment
options.C: Large open wards with minimal monitoring equipment
options.D: Focus primarily on long-term physical therapy and recovery

explanation: ICUs require specialized equipment and close nursing watch due to the extreme instability of the patients admitted there. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is a classic sign that a patient with diarrhoea is starting to get dehydrated?

options.A: Swelling in both lower legs and ankles
options.B: Dry mucous membranes and poor skin turgor
options.C: Excessive production of clear saliva
options.D: Increased blood pressure and flushed skin

explanation: When body fluid drops, tissues lose their bounce and moisture. Look out for a sticky dry mouth and skin that takes a moment to snap back when pinched!

question: What triggers the physical changes of puberty in teenage boys?

options.A: A sudden drop in core body temperature
options.B: A sudden surge in testosterone and related hormones
options.C: The full closure of the growth plates in long bones
options.D: An increase in the production of red blood cells

explanation: Spot on! A sudden rise in testosterone kicks off all those classic changes we see during adolescent growth.

question: Which physical finding is the classic hallmark of a patient with a vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Total absence of urine output for over 48 hours
options.B: Inability to walk due to paralysis of both legs
options.C: Severe lower abdominal swelling and tenderness
options.D: Continuous leakage of urine from the vaginal vault

explanation: You got it! Constant wetness is the tell-tale sign because urine flows straight into the vagina instead of collecting in the bladder. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h3)

question: Why is it so important to talk about family planning right after an abortion?

options.A: Patients lose natural immunity without hormonal birth control
options.B: Hormonal pills speed up physical recovery from a miscarriage
options.C: Fertility returns very quickly after an abortion procedure
options.D: Patients are required by law to start birth control immediately

explanation: Ovulation can happen as early as two weeks after an abortion! That means a patient can get pregnant again before their next period even arrives.

question: Which action using both hands is a leading cause of accidental needle-stick injuries among nurses?

options.A: Wiping skin with alcohol
options.B: Transporting safety boxes
options.C: Opening glass ampoules
options.D: Recapping used needles

explanation: Trying to guide a used needle back into its tiny cap with two hands is a classic hazard. That's why safety rules tell us never to recap used needles!

question: What is the best way to document your physical findings for an endocrine patient?

options.A: Document only the lab values and skip physical descriptions
options.B: Use general terms to save space in the medical record
options.C: Write personal opinions about the client's emotional state
options.D: Record objective and precise descriptions of physical signs

explanation: Clear, factual, and exact descriptions ensure that the whole healthcare team can track how the patient is doing over time without any guesswork.

question: What is the main functional difference between the front (anterior) and back (posterior) lobes of the pituitary gland?

options.A: The anterior lobe responds to nervous signals, while the posterior lobe responds exclusively to chemical blood signals
options.B: The anterior lobe synthesizes its own hormones, while the posterior lobe only stores and releases them
options.C: The posterior lobe produces releasing factors, while the anterior lobe targets the hypothalamus
options.D: The posterior lobe contains glandular epithelial cords, while the anterior lobe is made entirely of neurons

explanation: Remember: the anterior pituitary is a factory that makes its own hormones, while the posterior pituitary is more like a warehouse that just stores and sends out what the brain (hypothalamus) made for it!

question: When leaving an isolation room, what is the very first piece of PPE you take off?

options.A: Gloves
options.B: Goggles
options.C: Gown
options.D: Mask

explanation: Your gloves have touched the most germs, so they come off first! Always peel them off carefully before touching anything else.

question: What is the main reason for doing a neurological exam in a step-by-step head-to-toe order?

options.A: It ensures no critical part of the exam is missed.
options.B: It is the only legal requirement for documentation.
options.C: It prevents the patient from feeling any discomfort.
options.D: It shortens the total time needed for the shift.

explanation: Ward shifts get super busy! Following a steady routine keeps you organized so you never accidentally skip a vital step.

question: Why does a drop in estrogen during menopause lead to atrophic vaginitis?

options.A: It permanently closes the internal cervical os.
options.B: It thins the vaginal lining and reduces natural moisture and elasticity.
options.C: It triggers an allergic reaction to normal vaginal secretions.
options.D: It encourages the massive overgrowth of anaerobic bacteria.

explanation: You got it! Lower estrogen levels make the vaginal walls thinner, drier, and more fragile, which easily leads to irritation and inflammation.
